diagnosis.summary: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the 10:15 deployment, breaching the SLO. The issue is linked to the new database connection pool configuration introduced in the release.
diagnosis.root_cause: The migration to orders-client v3 reduced the database connection pool size to 10 connections, leading to connection pool exhaustion and increased latency.

evidence.finding: Production p95 latency is 2150 ms, breaching the SLO of 400 ms.
Staging p95 latency is 180 ms, well within the SLO of 400 ms.
The commit a91f3c2 removed database pool settings and set max_connections to 10.
Production database connection pool is fully utilized (in_use: 10, max_connections: 10) with 143 waiting connections.
Production acquire_wait_p95_ms is 1800 ms, indicating long waits for database connections.
All checkout-api pods in production are running version v4.17 and are healthy.
The deployment DEP-88213 introduced version v4.17 with the commit a91f3c2.

ruled_out: The staging environment running the same version does not exhibit the latency issue, ruling out a code-level bug.
The deployment did not affect other services, ruling out a shared infrastructure issue.

proposal.rationale: The Checkout API's p95 latency has increased to 2150 ms in production after the deployment of version v4.17, breaching the SLO. The root cause is the reduced database connection pool size to 10 connections, leading to connection pool exhaustion. Rolling back to the previous version, v4.16, will restore the original configuration and resolve the latency issue.
